correctness.rationale: Grouping Hardy coefficients by their residue j modulo k gives the orthogonal direct sum f(z)=sum_j z^j g_j(z^k). A unitary node DFT turns the evaluation map in sector j into two weighted evaluations of g_j at r^k and s^k exp(ikθ), the second with an irrelevant phase exp(ijθ). Their Gram matrix gives the claimed A_j,B_j,C_j and strictly positive determinant (the two sector points are distinct). After rephasing, each block is the previous one congruenced by diag(r,s). Its maximum decreases by the operator norm bound s²; testing the new block on the normalized inverse image of the old minimum eigenvector gives the same strict upper bound for its minimum. Thus sectors 0 and k−1 are extremal for all angles. At fixed diagonals both edges move strictly and oppositely with C_j, which is uniquely minimized at the half-step; the condition ratio follows. The minimum norm right inverse has norm λ_min^(−1/2), using the nonzero singular spectrum. At j=k−1 the top eigenvalue is asymptotic to B_j, and det/B_j is asymptotic to k(1−r²)r^(2k−2)s^(2k); at j=0 the matrix divided by k tends to a rank-one matrix of trace 2−r²−s². These prove the constants and the ratio for fixed distinct radii. The finite supplied checker was inspected, not run; its sampled comparisons are not needed for the proof.

value.rationale: For two prescribed radial sampling layers, worst-case minimum-norm interpolation and maximal evaluation gain are stricter objectives than a determinant. Their exact simultaneous optimum, and the sharp exponential conditioning that still remains there, matter for choosing and evaluating this natural design. The result does not optimize unrestricted node sets.
